sentences.text: Ornatops is a genus of saurolophine hadrosaur known as the "ornate face" that lived in the Upper Cretaceous of New Mexico.
The generic name Ornatops means "ornate face" and refers to the elaborate nasofrontal suture on the skull.
The exact body proportions of Ornatops remain undescribed because the original description only examined the cranial skeleton.
The species name incantatus means "enchanted" and references New Mexico's nickname, the "Land of Enchantment".
Ornatops is the first known crested brachylophosaurin found in southern Laramidia, highlighting the diversity of this group in North America during the Campanian.
The fossil material of Ornatops was first discovered in 2018 in the Menefee Formation of New Mexico.
The genus was formally described in 2021 based on the relatively complete and articulated holotype specimen WSC 10058.
The holotype includes a well-preserved skull without jaws, vertebrae, ribs, and limb bones, making it the most complete dinosaur found in the Menefee Formation.
McDonald et al. classify Ornatops within the subfamily Saurolophinae and the tribe Brachylophosaurini.
Ornatops lived approximately 78 million years ago in what is now New Mexico, United States.
Ornatops lived during the late Upper Cretaceous, specifically the Campanian stage, about 78 million years ago in North America.
The time range for Ornatops is recorded as the Campanian stage, spanning from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
